items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: The same way you'd ask me to compare Lloyd Glenn possibly with Eddie Hewitt, which is two different things all together.

ctx.x: But how would you describe him? Would you compare him with...

It's hard to compare an individual that has a style of his own. The same way you'd ask me to compare Lloyd Glenn possibly with Eddie Hewitt, which is two different things all together. Or the same with Peck Kelly. You couldn't say Peck was like so and so. Peck was like Peck Kelly. Was he fast? Yeah, very fast. Then you had Alan Vann that was with Troy's band. You can't compare him with Peck, but he played songs that Peck played too like Kitten on the Keys and things like that which was big in those days.
Did the Desdems ever get down there? Dan Desdems or Clarence Desdems? Did you ever meet them?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: And Eddie Hewitt's daddy would come through there. He was a piano player.

ctx.x: And who were some of the great Southwestern bands?

Well now there were quite a number of those bands and I just can't recall all of them. The two to the name were the outstanding ones, Troy and Trent. Of course in Galveston, Texas you had a band named Lazy Daddy's Band. Then you had the Royal Garden Band that left from Texas and went to California, which was another tremendous pioneer band. And Eddie Hewitt's daddy would come through there. He was a piano player. But there weren't too many big bands. Most of them concentrated on three, four and five piece combos.
What was the Royal Garden Band?
